questions.question: Rama packs 36 boxes in 1 h. Her sister needs 3 h to pack the same number. How much time will they together take to pack these 36 boxes?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Rama packs 36 boxes in 1 hour.

Her sister packs 36 boxes in 3 hours.

**Formula Used:**

Combined work rate = Sum of individual work rates

Time taken = Total work / Combined work rate

**Calculation:**

Rama's work rate = 36 boxes / 1 hour = 36 boxes/hour

Her sister's work rate = 36 boxes / 3 hours = 12 boxes/hour

Combined work rate = 36 boxes/hour + 12 boxes/hour = 48 boxes/hour

Time taken to pack 36 boxes together

Time = 36 boxes / 48 boxes/hour

Time = 3/4 hour

Time = 3/4 × 60 minutes

Time = 45 minutes

**The correct answer is option 4 (45 minutes).**

questions.question: When was the first population census conducted in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1872**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The first population census in India was conducted in the year **1872** during the British colonial rule.
 
• It was conducted under the supervision of **Henry Waterfield**, who was then the Census Commissioner of India.
 
• The census of 1872 was not synchronous, meaning it was not conducted at the same time across the country. Different regions conducted the census at different times.
 
• This census laid the foundation for a more systematic and regular decennial census that began from 1881.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Census**

 
 
• A census is a systematic and complete enumeration of the population.
 
• It typically records details about individuals such as age, sex, occupation, nationality, and other demographic information.
 
• Census data is crucial for planning and policy-making, providing a comprehensive picture of the population's characteristics and needs.
 
 
 
• **Decennial Census**
 
 
• The decennial census is conducted every ten years and aims to count every resident in the country.
 
• In India, the decennial census has been conducted regularly since 1881.
 
• It is the largest administrative exercise in the country and involves a vast number of enumerators and supervisors.
 
 
 
• **Henry Waterfield**
 
 
• Henry Waterfield was a British civil servant who played a significant role in organizing the first population census in India.
 
• He was the Census Commissioner of India during the 1872 census.
 
• His efforts were instrumental in laying the groundwork for future censuses in the country.
 
 
 
• **British Colonial Rule**
 
 
• The period during which the British Empire ruled over India, approximately from 1858 to 1947.
 
• The British introduced various administrative reforms, including the census, to better govern the population.
 
• The first census in 1872 was part of these administrative initiatives to gather detailed information about the Indian population.

questions.question: In which city was Gandhiji informed about the problems in Champaran and invited to visit the place?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lucknow**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Gandhiji was informed about the problems in Champaran by a farmer named Raj Kumar Shukla at the Lucknow session of the Indian National Congress in 1916.
 
• Raj Kumar Shukla was persistent in his request, urging Gandhiji to visit Champaran and see the plight of the farmers suffering under the oppressive system of Indigo plantation.
 
• The farmers in Champaran were forced to grow Indigo on a portion of their land and sell it at prices fixed by the British planters, leading to widespread exploitation.
 
• This invitation marked the beginning of the Champaran Satyagraha, which was Gandhiji's first active involvement in the Indian freedom struggle and a significant movement in Indian history.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Champaran Satyagraha**

 
 
• The Champaran Satyagraha of 1917 was the first Satyagraha movement led by Mahatma Gandhi in India.
 
• The farmers in the Champaran district of Bihar were being forced by British planters to grow Indigo under the tinkathia system, which was extremely exploitative.
 
• Gandhiji's intervention in Champaran was a turning point in the Indian freedom struggle as it highlighted the issues of rural India and mobilized the masses.
 
• The success of the Champaran Satyagraha established Gandhiji as a key leader in the Indian independence movement and demonstrated the power of non-violent resistance.
 
 
 
• **Indigo Plantation System**
 
 
• The Indigo plantation system was a form of agricultural exploitation practiced by the British in India, particularly in Bihar and Bengal.
 
• Farmers were coerced into planting Indigo on a fixed portion of their land and selling it at prices dictated by the British planters.
 
• This system led to severe economic hardship for the farmers as Indigo cultivation was less profitable compared to food crops.
 
• The oppressive nature of the Indigo plantation system was one of the key issues addressed by the Champaran Satyagraha.
 
 
 
• **Satyagraha**
 
 
• Satyagraha is a form of non-violent resistance or civil disobedience developed by Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• The term "Satyagraha" is derived from two Sanskrit words: "Satya" meaning truth and "Agraha" meaning insistence or holding firmly to.
 
• Gandhiji used Satyagraha as a tool to resist oppression and injustice through non-violent means, emphasizing the power of truth and moral righteousness.
 
• Satyagraha played a crucial role in the Indian independence movement and inspired various civil rights movements around the world.

questions.question: As per the census of 2011 which of the following is the highest populated state in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uttar Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

• As per the Census of 2011, **Uttar Pradesh** is the highest populated state in India with a population of approximately **199.81 million**.

questions.question: The ratio of two numbers is 3 : 5 and their LCM is 105. What is the difference between the numbers?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The ratio of two numbers is 3:5.

Their LCM is 105.

**Formula Used:**

Let the two numbers be 3x and 5x.

LCM of 3x and 5x = 15x

**Calculation:**

Given LCM is 105, so:

15x = 105

⇒ x = 105 / 15

⇒ x = 7

The two numbers are 3x and 5x:

3x = 3 × 7 = 21

5x = 5 × 7 = 35

Difference between the numbers:

Difference = 35 - 21

⇒ Difference = 14

**The difference between the numbers is 14.**

questions.question: What is the ratio of nitrogen and hydrogen in ammonia on the basis of mass ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**14 : 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The chemical formula of ammonia is NH₃.
 
• In one molecule of ammonia, there is one nitrogen (N) atom and three hydrogen (H) atoms.
 
• The atomic mass of nitrogen is 14 units, while the atomic mass of hydrogen is 1 unit.
 
• Therefore, the total mass of hydrogen in NH₃ is 3 units (3 x 1), making the ratio of nitrogen to hydrogen in ammonia 14:3 by mass.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ammonia (NH₃)**

 
 
• Ammonia is a compound of nitrogen and hydrogen with the formula NH₃.
 
• It is a colorless gas with a characteristic pungent smell.
 
• Ammonia is a building-block chemical and a key component in the manufacture of many products people use every day.
 
• It is primarily used in the production of fertilizers, which is crucial for food production.
 
 
 
• **Atomic Mass**
 
 
• Atomic mass is the mass of an atomic particle, sub-atomic particle, or molecule.
 
• It is commonly expressed in unified atomic mass units (u), where 1 u is defined as one twelfth of the mass of a carbon-12 atom.
 
• The atomic mass of an element is approximately equivalent to the number of protons and neutrons in the atom (the mass number).
 
 
 
• **Chemical Formula**
 
 
• A chemical formula is a way of presenting information about the chemical proportions of atoms that constitute a particular chemical compound or molecule.
 
• It uses chemical element symbols, numbers, and sometimes also other symbols, such as parentheses, dashes, brackets, commas, and plus (+) and minus (−) signs.
 
• For example, the formula of water is H₂O, indicating it has two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.
 
 
 
• **Molecular Mass**
 
 
• Molecular mass is the mass of a given molecule and is calculated as the sum of the atomic masses of all the atoms in the molecule.
 
• It is typically measured in atomic mass units (u).
 
• For instance, the molecular mass of NH₃ (ammonia) is 17 u (14 u from nitrogen and 3 u from hydrogen).

questions.question: How many basic elements (Tatvas) have been described by early Indian philosophers to classify matter?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Five**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Early Indian philosophers classified matter into five basic elements known as "Panchamahabhutas".
 
• These five elements are Earth (Prithvi), Water (Jal), Fire (Agni), Air (Vayu), and Ether/Space (Akasha).
 
• This classification is fundamental to various Indian philosophies including Ayurveda, Yoga, and Sankhya.
 
• Each of these elements represents different states of matter and energy in the physical and metaphysical universe.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Panchamahabhutas**

 
 
• In Sanskrit, "Panchamahabhutas" translates to "five great elements".
 
• **Earth (Prithvi)**: Represents solidity and stability. It is associated with the sense of smell.
 
• **Water (Jal)**: Represents fluidity and is essential for life. It is associated with the sense of taste.
 
• **Fire (Agni)**: Represents transformation and energy. It is associated with the sense of sight.
 
• **Air (Vayu)**: Represents movement and is associated with the sense of touch.
 
• **Ether/Space (Akasha)**: Represents the space in which everything exists and is associated with the sense of sound.
 
 
 
• **Ayurveda**
 
 
• An ancient Indian system of medicine that relies heavily on the concept of Panchamahabhutas for diagnosis and treatment.
 
• It aims to balance the five elements within the body to maintain health and wellness.
 
 
 
• **Yoga**
 
 
• In Yoga, the five elements are considered to be the building blocks of the universe, including the human body.
 
• Practices such as asanas (postures) and pranayama (breathing exercises) are used to balance these elements.
 
 
 
• **Sankhya Philosophy**
 
 
• An ancient Indian school of philosophy that explains the creation of the universe through the interaction of Purusha (consciousness) and Prakriti (matter), which includes the Panchamahabhutas.

questions.question: According to Article 170, the number of seats in the Legislative Assembly of each State should not be more than _______.

__
 
• Article 170 of the Indian Constitution pertains to the composition of the Legislative Assemblies in Indian states.

• **Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha):**
 
 
• The Legislative Assembly is the lower house of the state legislature in India.
 
• Members of the Legislative Assembly (MLAs) are elected directly by the people from single-member constituencies.
 
• The term of the Legislative Assembly is five years unless dissolved sooner.
 
• The size of the Legislative Assembly varies from state to state, depending on the population.

• Not all states have a Legislative Council; it exists only in certain states as per the provisions of the Constitution.
 
• The Council acts as a revising chamber, providing a second opinion on bills passed by the Legislative Assembly.
 
 
 
• **Delimitation:**
 
 
• Delimitation refers to the act of redrawing the boundaries of electoral constituencies to reflect changes in population.
 
• This process ensures that each constituency has roughly the same number of inhabitants, maintaining fair representation.
 
• The Delimitation Commission is appointed by the President of India and works in collaboration with the Election Commission.

Data set: 3, 4, 5, 6, 7

Standard Deviation (SD) = √(Σ(x - mean)² / N)

Where,

Σ represents the sum of all values

x is each value in the dataset

mean is the average of the dataset

N is the total number of data points

Mean = (3 + 4 + 5 + 6 + 7) / 5

Mean = 25 / 5

Mean = 5

(3 - 5)² = (-2)² = 4

(5 - 5)² = (0)² = 0

(6 - 5)² = (1)² = 1

(7 - 5)² = (2)² = 4

We need to find the greatest number of four digits which is divisible by 18, 25, 45, and 55.

**Formula Used:**

**Calculation:**

Prime factorization:

18 = 2 × 3²

25 = 5²

45 = 3² × 5

55 = 5 × 11

⇒ LCM = 2 × 9 × 275

⇒ LCM = 2 × 2475

⇒ LCM = 4950

The largest four-digit number is 9999. To find the greatest number of four digits divisible by 4950, we divide 9999 by 4950 and find the quotient.

Quotient = 9999 / 4950

⇒ Quotient ≈ 2

Therefore, the greatest number of four digits which is divisible by 4950 is 4950 × 2 = 9900.

**The correct answer is option 3, 9900.**

questions.question: Which of the following British policies triggered people to assemble at Jallianwala Bagh, Amritsar?

__
 
• The Rowlatt Act, also known as the Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act of 1919, was passed by the British government in India in March 1919.
 
• The act gave the British authorities the power to imprison any person suspected of terrorism living in British India without trial for up to two years.
 
• The act also allowed the British government to stop the press from reporting and to arrest individuals suspected of sedition without a warrant.
 
• The widespread anger against the Rowlatt Act led to a series of protests and gatherings, which culminated in the tragic Jallianwala Bagh massacre.

• This act introduced a dual mode of administration, called dyarchy, in the provinces of British India.
 
• It was part of the Montagu-Chelmsford reforms and aimed to increase the participation of Indians in the government.
 
• The act divided the subjects of administration into two categories: transferred and reserved subjects.
 
• While transferred subjects were to be administered by ministers accountable to the Legislative Council, reserved subjects were to be administered by the Governor and his executive council.
 
 
 
• **Simon Commission**

• It arrived in India in 1928 to study constitutional reform and make recommendations.
 
• However, the commission faced a widespread boycott because it did not include any Indian members.
 
• The commission's arrival led to protests and further fueled the demand for self-rule in India.
 
 
 
• **The Pitts India Act 1784**
 
 
• This act was passed to address the shortcomings of the Regulating Act of 1773.
 
• It established the dual control of the British government and the East India Company over India.
 
• The act set up a Board of Control in Britain to oversee the civil, military, and revenue affairs of the company.
 
• This act is significant as it marked the beginning of British parliamentary control over the East India Company’s activities in India.

questions.question: What is the standard noise level proposed by the Central Board for Pollution Control for residential areas during the night?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**45db**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Central Board for Pollution Control (CPCB) has set the standard noise level for residential areas at night to be **45 decibels (dB)**.
 
• This standard is meant to ensure a peaceful and quiet environment during night-time hours, which is critical for the health and well-being of residents.
 
• The night-time hours, as defined by CPCB, are from **10 PM to 6 AM**.
 
• Noise levels above 45 dB in residential areas during the night can be considered as noise pollution and are subject to regulatory actions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Central Board for Pollution Control (CPCB)**

 
 
• The CPCB is a statutory organization under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC).
 
• It was established in 1974 under the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974, and was entrusted with powers and functions under the Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981.
 
• The CPCB provides technical services to the MoEFCC on matters related to pollution control and environmental conservation.
 
• It also lays down standards for the prevention and control of noise pollution in India.
 
 
 
• **Noise Pollution**
 
 
• Noise pollution refers to unwanted or harmful sounds that disrupt the natural balance of human and animal life.
 
• Common sources include traffic, industrial processes, construction activities, and loudspeakers.
 
• Prolonged exposure to high noise levels can lead to health issues such as stress, hearing loss, and sleep disturbances.
 
• The CPCB's regulations aim to minimize these impacts by setting permissible noise levels for different areas and times of the day.
 
 
 
• **Decibel (dB)**
 
 
• Decibel is a unit used to measure the intensity of sound.
 
• The scale is logarithmic, meaning a small increase in dB represents a large increase in intensity.
 
• A normal conversation is typically around 60 dB, while a quiet library is around 40 dB.
 
• The CPCB uses dB as the standard unit for setting permissible noise levels.

questions.question: Two regular polygons have the same number of sides. Their lengths are in the ratio 7 : 5 and the area of the larger polygon is 1127 cm². Find the area of the smaller polygon.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Ratio of side lengths of the two polygons = 7 : 5

Area of the larger polygon = 1127 cm²

**Formula Used:**

The area of similar polygons is proportional to the square of the ratio of their corresponding side lengths.

**Calculation:**

Let the side lengths of the larger and smaller polygons be 7x and 5x respectively.

Ratio of areas of the polygons = (7x / 5x)²

Ratio of areas = (7 / 5)²

Ratio of areas = 49 / 25

Let the area of the smaller polygon be A cm².

Then, 1127 / A = 49 / 25

⇒ A = 1127 × 25 / 49

⇒ A = 23 × 25

⇒ A = 575 cm²

**The area of the smaller polygon is 575 cm².**

questions.question: If with simple interest, an amount doubles in 5 years, how many times of the original amount, will it be after 8 years with same rate of simple interest?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The amount doubles in 5 years with simple interest.

We need to find how many times of the original amount it will be after 8 years with the same rate of interest.

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest = (P × R × T)/100

Calculations:

In simple interest, the interest is directly proportional to both the principal amount and the time period.

If the amount doubles in 5 years, we can assume:

Principal = P

Amount after 5 years = 2P

Time = 5 years

So, the interest earned in 5 years is:

Interest = Amount - Principal = 2P - P = P

The rate of interest (R) can be calculated as:

R = (Interest) / (Principal × Time)

R = P / (P × 5) = 1/5 × 100 = 20%

Now, we need to calculate the amount after 8 years with the same rate of interest (20%).

Interest for 8 years = P × (20/100) × 8 = 1.6P

Thus, the total amount after 8 years:

Amount = Principal + Interest = P + 1.6P = 2.6P

**∴ After 8 years, the amount will be 2.6 times the original amount.**

questions.question: If one angle of a parallelogram is 12° less than twice the smallest angle of the same parallelogram, then the largest angle of the parallelogram is :
questions.solution:
**Given:**

One angle of a parallelogram is 12º less than twice the smallest angle of the same parallelogram.

**Formula Used:**

Sum of adjacent angles in a parallelogram = 180º

**Calculation:**

Let the smallest angle be x degrees.

The other angle is 2x - 12º.

Since adjacent angles in a parallelogram sum up to 180º:

⇒ x + (2x - 12) = 180

⇒ 3x - 12 = 180

⇒ 3x = 192

⇒ x = 64

So, the smallest angle is 64º.

The other angle is 2x - 12 = 2(64) - 12 = 128 - 12 = 116º .

The largest angle in a parallelogram is 180º - smallest angle:

⇒ 180º - 64º = 116º.

**The largest angle of the parallelogram is 116º.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The system consists of a constellation of at least 24 satellites orbiting the Earth, ground control stations, and GPS receivers used by individuals.

questions.question: In which of the following plants is the body NOT differentiated into roots, stems and leaves?

questions.question: Which movement is called India's first Civil Disobedience Movement?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Champaran Movement**__.

__
 
• The Champaran Movement of 1917 is considered India's first civil disobedience movement led by Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• It was initiated to address the grievances of the farmers who were forced to grow indigo under oppressive conditions by the British planters.
 
• Gandhi's involvement in the movement marked his first significant experiment with non-violent resistance or Satyagraha in India.
 
• The success of the Champaran Movement laid the foundation for future civil disobedience campaigns against British rule in India.

• Launched by Mahatma Gandhi in 1920, it aimed at non-violent resistance to British rule by boycotting British goods, institutions, and services.
 
• The movement saw widespread participation and led to several significant events, including the Jallianwala Bagh massacre.
 
 
 
• **Khilafat Movement**
 
 
• A pan-Islamist movement launched in 1919 to protest against the dismemberment of the Ottoman Caliphate by the British after World War I.
 
• Gandhi supported the movement to bring Hindu-Muslim unity in the struggle against British colonial rule.
 
 
 
• **Kheda Movement**
 
 
• Another significant peasant movement led by Mahatma Gandhi in 1918 in Gujarat.
 
• It was launched to support farmers who were unable to pay taxes due to crop failure and sought remission of taxes.
